candidates.name: Maya Fitzgerald

strengths.text: Genuinely curious in every conversation, asked follow-up questions
Already volunteering at Tampa General on weekends

facts: Pre-Med track, considering EM or peds
Volunteers at Tampa General General ED
Former high school EMT cadet program

notes.text: Asked me three follow-up questions about how I balance shadowing with classes. Genuinely engaged, not just being polite.
She's already doing ED volunteer hours at TGH. Talked about a specific patient interaction that stuck with her.
Comfortable talking to everyone at the table, not just me. Good energy.
Asked good questions about our service events specifically, seemed like she'd looked us up beforehand.
Mentioned the EMT cadet thing unprompted when I asked about her interest in EM.

candidates.name: Derek Osei

concerns.text: Still very unsure about even applying to dental school

facts: Interested in dentistry but hasn't shadowed yet

notes.text: Nice guy, easy conversation, but when I asked what drew him to dental he said 'my dentist growing up was cool.' Very early stage.
Admitted he hasn't shadowed anyone yet and isn't sure if he wants dental or PA. Fine for a freshman, just early.

candidates.name: Isabella Cruz

strengths.text: Strong clinical background — works as a CNA on weekends

concerns.text: Came across as reciting a resume rather than having a real conversation

observations.text: Warmed up a lot once we talked about her actual patients, really personable underneath the nerves.
Felt stiff and rehearsed the whole time, like she was interviewing for a job.

facts: Works as a CNA at a local skilled nursing facility
Applying to PA programs next cycle

notes.text: CNA experience is real and substantial — she talked about specific patients with a lot of care. Nervous at first but opened up.
Very qualified on paper. Conversation felt a little transactional but her experience speaks for itself.
Felt like she was running through talking points. Didn't feel like a natural conversation.
Same read as Jordan — very polished but stiff. Hard to get a sense of who she actually is.
Only got a few minutes with him before rotation ended. Seemed polite, mentioned he wants to do large-animal vet work eventually. Need more notes on him.

candidates.name: Grace Whitfield

strengths.text: Excellent listener, made the conversation feel two-way

concerns.text: Referral source unclear — didn't know much about the chapter going in

facts: Involved in campus mental health advocacy group

notes.text: Really easy to talk to, asked about my actual experience in the chapter rather than generic questions.
Good listener, remembered details from earlier in the conversation and circled back to them.
Didn't seem to know much about us coming in, but engaged well once we started talking. Not a red flag, just early awareness.

candidates.name: Nathaniel Osborn

concerns.text: Dismissive tone when talking to brothers who weren't in leadership positions
Name-dropped connections rather than talking about himself

facts: Interned at a sports medicine clinic last summer

notes.text: Barely looked at me while talking, kept scanning the room for who else was there. Spent most of the conversation name-dropping people he knows in the chapter already.
Similar experience — noticeably more engaged once he found out I was on exec.
Same pattern I've heard from others. Not rude exactly, just clearly sorting people by perceived importance.
Good internship experience but the conversation was mostly him telling me who he knows.

candidates.name: Priya Ramaswamy

strengths.text: Thoughtful about why professional fraternity vs. social
Already researching MCAT prep timeline as a freshman

facts: Planning to shadow a family friend who's an IM physician this summer

notes.text: Explained clearly why she wanted a professional org specifically over a social sorority. Mature perspective for a freshman.
Same — she'd clearly thought about what she wanted out of this before coming tonight.
Already has an MCAT prep timeline sketched out. Ambitious but not showing off about it.

candidates.name: Connor Delacroix

strengths.text: Direct and honest about still exploring options

concerns.text: Very quiet, hard to draw into conversation

facts: Transferred from a community college this year

notes.text: Had to pull most answers out of him, but when he did talk he was honest — said he's still deciding between PA and pharmacy.
Very reserved. Could be nerves, could be genuine disinterest. Hard to tell from one conversation.
